<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Here's what I found in the codebase, plus my recommendations.

## Important technical wrinkle first

DiscDock currently treats "Audio CD" scans as **metadata cataloging only** — [audioCd.ts](electron/scanning/audioCd.ts) reads the TOC and MusicBrainz info, and [scanManager.ts](electron/scanning/scanManager.ts#L118-L131) writes synthetic file records like `01 - Song Title.cdda` with no real path — there's no actual audio data behind them. That's very different from an **MP3/data CD**, which has real files on a real filesystem.

That means "play an audio/mp3 CD" is really two features:
1. **MP3 CD (data disc with audio files)** — easy: real file path exists, stream it to an `<audio>` element via a small IPC/protocol handler. Low effort.
2. **True Audio CD (CDDA, raw sectors)** — hard: there's no accessible file. Playback requires shelling out to something like `cdparanoia`/`ffmpeg` to rip the track to a temp WAV/stream in real time and feed it to the renderer. This also depends on the same optional Linux tools noted in my memory (`cd-info`/`cdparanoia`) not being reliably present, and device/eject code for Windows/macOS is already flagged untested — CD audio extraction on those platforms is a bigger unknown.

I'd like to confirm scope before building, since it changes the effort a lot. 

Now export `resolveLivePath` from files.ts: 

Both projects type-check cleanly. Now let's check `Readable.toWeb` types compile (Node lib) — it passed, good. Let's also verify `button--icon-only` and `link-button`/`button` base classes exist for styling consistency, and quickly run the app build to be extra sure (vite build + electron compile via existing npm scripts).

const CDDA_BYTES_PER_SECTOR = 2352
const CDDA_SECTORS_PER_SECOND = 75
// Audio CD track offsets are expressed from the start of the disc, which begins at sector 150.
const CDDA_LEADIN_SECTORS = 150

const MISSING_TOOLS_MESSAGE =
  'Reading audio CDs needs a CD tool that DiscDock does not bundle. Install one, then try again:\n' +
  '  Debian/Ubuntu/Mint:  sudo apt install libcdio-utils cdparanoia\n' +
  '  Fedora/RHEL:         sudo dnf install libcdio cdparanoia\n' +
  '  Arch:                sudo pacman -S libcdio cdparanoia'

const NO_DISC_MESSAGE = 'No disc detected in the drive — insert an audio CD and try again.'

/** True when the failure is "the binary is not installed" rather than a read error. */
function isMissingBinary(err: unknown): boolean {
  const error = err as NodeJS.ErrnoException & { stderr?: string }
  return error.code === 'ENOENT' || /not found/i.test(error.stderr ?? '')
}

function isEmptyDrive(err: unknown): boolean {
  const detail = (err as Error & { stderr?: string; stdout?: string })
  const text = `${detail.stderr ?? ''}${detail.stdout ?? ''}${detail.message ?? ''}`
  return /no medium|no disc|can't get first track|not ready/i.test(text)
}

function sectorsToSeconds(sectors: number): number {
  return Math.round(sectors / CDDA_SECTORS_PER_SECOND)
}

function toTrack(trackNumber: number, startSector: number, sectors: number, isAudio: boolean): AudioCdTrack {
  return {
    trackNumber,
    startSector,
    sectors,
    durationSeconds: sectorsToSeconds(sectors),
    sizeBytes: sectors * CDDA_BYTES_PER_SECTOR,
    isAudio
  }
}

function formatBytes(bytes: number): string {
  if (bytes === 0) return '0 B'
  const units = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB']
  const exponent = Math.min(Math.floor(Math.log(bytes) / Math.log(1024)), units.length - 1)
  return `${(bytes / 1024 ** exponent).toFixed(1)} ${units[exponent]}`
}

function formatDuration(seconds: number): string {
  const minutes = Math.floor(seconds / 60)
  return `${minutes}:${String(seconds % 60).padStart(2, '0')}`
}

  mediaId: number
  onBack: () => void
}

Here's what I found in the codebase, plus my recommendations.

## Important technical wrinkle first

DiscDock currently treats "Audio CD" scans as **metadata cataloging only** — `electron/scanning/audioCd.ts` reads the TOC and MusicBrainz info, and `electron/scanning/scanManager.ts#L118-L131` writes synthetic file 

 writes synthetic file records like `01 - Song Title.cdda` with no real path — there's no actual audio data behind them. That's very different from an **MP3/data CD**, which has real files on a real filesystem.

That means "play an audio/mp3 CD" is really two features:
1. **MP3 CD (data disc with audio files)** — easy: real file path exists, stream it to an `<audio>` element via a small IPC/protocol handler. Low effort.
2. **True Audio CD (CDDA, raw sectors)** — hard: there's no accessible file. Playback requires shelling out to something like `cdparanoia`/`ffmpeg` to rip the track to a temp WAV/stream in real time and feed it to the renderer. This also depends on the same optional Linux tools noted in my memory (`cd-info`/`cdparanoia`) not being reliably present, and device/eject code for Windows/macOS is already flagged untested — CD audio extraction on those platforms is a bigger unknown.

I'd like to confirm scope before building, since it changes the effort a lot.

/** Looks up a single cataloged file's kind, used to gate playback to audio-kind entries only. */
export function getFileKind(mediaItemId: number, filePath: string): string | null {
  const row = getDb()
    .prepare(
      `SELECT kind FROM file_record WHERE media_item_id = @mediaItemId AND path = @filePath AND is_directory = 0`
    )
    .get({ mediaItemId, filePath }) as { kind: string } | undefined
  return row?.kind ?? null
}

import { protocol } from 'electron'
import fs from 'node:fs'
import { Readable } from 'node:stream'
import { getFileKind } from '../db/fileRepository'
import { resolveLivePath } from './files'

/** Custom scheme the renderer's <audio> element streams cataloged audio files through. */
export const AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME = 'discdock-media'

function guessAudioMimeType(filePath: string): string {
  const ext = filePath.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase()
  switch (ext) {
    case 'mp3':
      return 'audio/mpeg'
    case 'wav':
      return 'audio/wav'
    case 'flac':
      return 'audio/flac'
    case 'ogg':
      return 'audio/ogg'
    case 'm4a':
    case 'aac':
      return 'audio/aac'
    case 'opus':
      return 'audio/opus'
    default:
      return 'application/octet-stream'
  }
}

/** Must be called before app.whenReady(), pairs with registerAudioStreamProtocol(). */
export function registerAudioStreamSchemePrivileges(): void {
  protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged([
    { scheme: AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME, privileges: { stream: true, supportFetchAPI: true, corsEnabled: true } }
  ])
}

/**
 * Serves cataloged audio files at discdock-media://<mediaId>/<encoded relative path>, with
 * Range support so <audio> can seek. Only files cataloged with kind 'audio' are served.
 */
export function registerAudioStreamProtocol(): void {
  protocol.handle(AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME, async (request) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(request.url)
      const mediaId = Number(url.hostname)
      const filePath = decodeURIComponent(url.pathname.slice(1))
      if (!Number.isInteger(mediaId) || mediaId <= 0 || !filePath) {
        return new Response('Invalid audio request', { status: 400 })
      }
      if (getFileKind(mediaId, filePath) !== 'audio') {
        return new Response('Not an audio file', { status: 403 })
      }

      const resolved = await resolveLivePath(mediaId, filePath)
      const stat = await fs.promises.stat(resolved)

      let start = 0
      let end = stat.size - 1
      let status = 200
      const headers: Record<string, string> = {
        'Content-Type': guessAudioMimeType(resolved),
        'Accept-Ranges': 'bytes'
      }

      const range = request.headers.get('range')
      if (range) {
        const match = /bytes=(\d*)-(\d*)/.exec(range)
        if (match && (match[1] || match[2])) {
          if (match[1]) start = Number(match[1])
          if (match[2]) end = Number(match[2])
          status = 206
          headers['Content-Range'] = `bytes ${start}-${end}/${stat.size}`
        }
      }

      headers['Content-Length'] = String(end - start + 1)
      const nodeStream = fs.createReadStream(resolved, { start, end })
      return new Response(Readable.toWeb(nodeStream) as ReadableStream, { status, headers })
    } catch (err) {
      return new Response(`Audio stream error: ${(err as Error).message}`, { status: 404 })
    }
  })
}

```

import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react'

export interface PlayerTrack {
  mediaId: number
  mediaLabel: string
  path: string
  name: string
  durationSeconds: number | null
}

interface PlayerState {
  queue: PlayerTrack[]
  currentIndex: number
  isPlaying: boolean
  currentTime: number
  duration: number
  volume: number
}

interface PlayerContextValue extends PlayerState {
  currentTrack: PlayerTrack | null
  play: (tracks: PlayerTrack[], startIndex: number) => void
  toggle: () => void
  next: () => void
  previous: () => void
  seek: (seconds: number) => void
  setVolume: (volume: number) => void
  close: () => void
}

const PlayerContext = createContext<PlayerContextValue | null>(null)

function trackUrl(track: PlayerTrack): string {
  return `discdock-media://${track.mediaId}/${encodeURIComponent(track.path)}`
}

export function PlayerProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }): JSX.Element {
  const audioRef = useRef<HTMLAudioElement | null>(null)
  const [state, setState] = useState<PlayerState>({
    queue: [],
    currentIndex: -1,
    isPlaying: false,
    currentTime: 0,
    duration: 0,
    volume: 1
  })

  if (!audioRef.current && typeof Audio !== 'undefined') {
    audioRef.current = new Audio()
  }

  const currentTrack = state.currentIndex >= 0 ? (state.queue[state.currentIndex] ?? null) : null

  const next = useCallback(() => {
    setState((prev) => {
      if (prev.currentIndex + 1 >= prev.queue.length) return { ...prev, isPlaying: false }
      return { ...prev, currentIndex: prev.currentIndex + 1, currentTime: 0 }
    })
  }, [])

  useEffect(() => {
    const audio = audioRef.current
    if (!audio) return

    const handleTimeUpdate = (): void => setState((prev) => ({ ...prev, currentTime: audio.currentTime }))
    const handleLoadedMetadata = (): void => setState((prev) => ({ ...prev, duration: audio.duration || 0 }))
    const handleEnded = (): void => next()

    audio.addEventListener('timeupdate', handleTimeUpdate)
    audio.addEventListener('loadedmetadata', handleLoadedMetadata)
    audio.addEventListener('ended', handleEnded)
    return () => {
      audio.removeEventListener('timeupdate', handleTimeUpdate)
      audio.removeEventListener('loadedmetadata', handleLoadedMetadata)
      audio.removeEventListener('ended', handleEnded)
    }
  }, [next])

  useEffect(() => {
    const audio = audioRef.current
    if (!audio || !currentTrack) return
    audio.src = trackUrl(currentTrack)
    audio.currentTime = 0
    if (state.isPlaying) void audio.play().catch(() => setState((prev) => ({ ...prev, isPlaying: false })))
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [currentTrack?.mediaId, currentTrack?.path])

  useEffect(() => {
    const audio = audioRef.current
    if (!audio) return
    if (state.isPlaying) void audio.play().catch(() => setState((prev) => ({ ...prev, isPlaying: false })))
    else audio.pause()
  }, [state.isPlaying])

  useEffect(() => {
    if (audioRef.current) audioRef.current.volume = state.volume
  }, [state.volume])

  const play = useCallback((tracks: PlayerTrack[], startIndex: number) => {
    setState((prev) => ({ ...prev, queue: tracks, currentIndex: startIndex, currentTime: 0, isPlaying: true }))
  }, [])

  const toggle = useCallback(() => {
    setState((prev) => (prev.currentIndex < 0 ? prev : { ...prev, isPlaying: !prev.isPlaying }))
  }, [])

  const previous = useCallback(() => {
    setState((prev) => {
      if (prev.currentIndex <= 0) return { ...prev, currentTime: 0 }
      return { ...prev, currentIndex: prev.currentIndex - 1, currentTime: 0 }
    })
  }, [])

  const seek = useCallback((seconds: number) => {
    if (audioRef.current) audioRef.current.currentTime = seconds
    setState((prev) => ({ ...prev, currentTime: seconds }))
  }, [])

  const setVolume = useCallback((volume: number) => {
    setState((prev) => ({ ...prev, volume }))
  }, [])

  const close = useCallback(() => {
    if (audioRef.current) {
      audioRef.current.pause()
      audioRef.current.removeAttribute('src')
    }
    setState({ queue: [], currentIndex: -1, isPlaying: false, currentTime: 0, duration: 0, volume: state.volume })
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [])

  const value = useMemo<PlayerContextValue>(
    () => ({ ...state, currentTrack, play, toggle, next, previous, seek, setVolume, close }),
    [state, currentTrack, play, toggle, next, previous, seek, setVolume, close]
  )

  return <PlayerContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</PlayerContext.Provider>
}

export function usePlayer(): PlayerContextValue {
  const ctx = useContext(PlayerContext)
  if (!ctx) throw new Error('usePlayer must be used within a PlayerProvider')
  return ctx
}

```

import { Pause, Play, SkipBack, SkipForward, Volume2, X } from 'lucide-react'
import { usePlayer } from '../player/PlayerContext'
import './PlayerBar.css'

function formatTime(seconds: number): string {
  if (!Number.isFinite(seconds) || seconds < 0) return '0:00'
  const mins = Math.floor(seconds / 60)

export default function PlayerBar(): JSX.Element | null {

          <SkipForward size={16} aria-hidden="true" />

          value={currentTime}
          onChange={(e) => seek(Number(e.target.value))}

        />
        <span className="player-bar__time">{formatTime(duration || currentTrack.durationSeconds || 0)}</span>

}

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

## Summary

Built a persistent, app-wide audio player (Phase 1: real files — MP3/data discs) and wired in the two placements you asked about:

**Where playback controls live:**
- **Global bottom mini-player bar** (, docked below the sidebar/content area, visible on every view once something is playing) — play/pause, prev/next, seek, volume, close. This is the persistent control surface so users don't lose it when navigating away.
- **Media Detail → Browse tab**: a Play button per audio-kind row; clicking queues all audio files in that folder starting from the clicked track.
- **Media Library**: a "Play Audio" item in the row's right-click menu, which grabs the disc's audio files and starts the queue.
- **Dashboard**: deliberately skipped — a freshly-detected device has nothing playable until it's scanned, so there's no natural trigger point there.

**Important caveat surfaced during investigation:** Audio CD (raw CDDA) scans only catalog *metadata* today — the "tracks" are synthetic records with no real audio data behind them. Real audio-CD playback needs live ripping (cdparanoia/ffmpeg) streamed to the renderer, which is a separate, larger follow-up. What's playable right now is anything with a real file path — MP3/data discs, or CD-Text/scanned audio files.

**Backend added:** a privileged `discdock-media://` protocol in Electron (Range-request support for seeking), gated to `kind === 'audio'` files only, reusing existing path-resolution/security checks. CSP updated accordingly. Full `npm run build` (renderer + electron) passes clean.

import { app, BrowserWindow, shell } from 'electron'
import path from 'node:path'
import { loadWindowState, trackWindowState } from './windowState'

const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'

export function createMainWindow(): BrowserWindow {
  const savedState = loadWindowState()

  const win = new BrowserWindow({
    width: savedState.width,
    height: savedState.height,
    x: savedState.x,
    y: savedState.y,
    minWidth: 900,
    minHeight: 600,
    // Frameless: DiscDock renders its own title bar/toolbar and window controls.
    frame: false,
    backgroundColor: '#1e1e1e',
    show: false,
    webPreferences: {
      preload: path.join(__dirname, '../preload.js'),
      contextIsolation: true,
      nodeIntegration: false,
      sandbox: true
    }
  })

  win.once('ready-to-show', () => {
    if (savedState.maximized) win.maximize()
    win.show()
  })

  trackWindowState(win)

  // Never allow navigation to or opening of remote content from the renderer.
  win.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler(({ url }) => {
    void shell.openExternal(url)
    return { action: 'deny' }
  })

  // DevTools are not opened automatically; toggle manually with Ctrl+Shift+I.
  // Restart is bound to Ctrl+Shift+R. Only react to keyDown — before-input-event also fires
  // on keyUp, which would otherwise double-fire (e.g. toggle open then immediately close again).
  win.webContents.on('before-input-event', (_event, input) => {
    if (input.type !== 'keyDown' || !input.control || !input.shift) return
    const key = input.key.toLowerCase()
    if (key === 'i') {
      win.webContents.toggleDevTools()
    } else if (key === 'r') {
      app.relaunch()
      app.exit(0)
    }
  })

  if (isDev) {
    void win.loadURL('http://localhost:5173')
  } else {
    void win.loadFile(path.join(__dirname, '../../../dist/index.html'))
  }
```

import log from 'electron-log/main'
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'
import { app } from 'electron'

export function initializeLogging(): void {
  const logsDirectory = path.join(app.getPath('userData'), 'logs')
  fs.mkdirSync(logsDirectory, { recursive: true })
  log.transports.file.resolvePathFn = () => path.join(logsDirectory, 'main.log')
  log.transports.file.level = 'info'
  log.info('DiscDock starting', { version: app.getVersion(), platform: process.platform })

  process.on('uncaughtException', (error) => {
    log.error('Uncaught main-process exception', error)
  })
  process.on('unhandledRejection', (reason) => {
    log.error('Unhandled main-process rejection', reason)
  })
}

export function logShutdown(): void {
  log.info('DiscDock shutting down')
}

export { log }

/**
 * Looks up a single cataloged file's kind, used to gate playback to real audio-kind entries.
 * Audio-CD scans catalog synthetic `.cdda` track placeholders with no underlying file, so those
 * are excluded even though they're marked kind 'audio'.
 */
export function getFileKind(mediaItemId: number, filePath: string): string | null {
  const row = getDb()
    .prepare(
      `SELECT kind, extension FROM file_record
       WHERE media_item_id = @mediaItemId AND path = @filePath AND is_directory = 0`
    )
    .get({ mediaItemId, filePath }) as { kind: string; extension: string | null } | undefined
  if (!row || row.extension === 'cdda') return null
  return row.kind
```

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

**Root cause found and fixed:** the 404 was DiscDock's new Play button trying to stream an Audio-CD's synthetic `.cdda` track placeholder — those catalog entries have `kind: 'audio'` but no real file behind them, so the streaming protocol handler failed and the renderer reported it as a 404.

**Fix:** added  to , and now exclude `extension === 'cdda'` both server-side ( in `electron/db/fileRepository.ts`) and in the Play-button filters in `src/views/MediaDetail.tsx` and `src/views/MediaLibrary.tsx`. Real MP3/data-disc files still play fine; Audio-CD (CDDA) tracks no longer show a Play affordance since they genuinely can't be played without the (not-yet-built) live-ripping feature. Full build passes clean.

function runMigrations(database: Database.Database): void {
  database.pragma('foreign_keys = ON')
  database.pragma('journal_mode = WAL')
  database.exec('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)')

  )

  for (const migration of MIGRATIONS) {
    if (appliedVersions.has(migration.version)) continue
    log.info('Applying database migration', { version: migration.version })
    const applyMigration = database.transaction(() => {
      database.exec(migration.sql)
      database
        .prepare('INSERT INTO schema_migrations (version) VALUES (?)')
        .run(migration.version)
    })
    applyMigration()
    log.info('Database migration applied', { version: migration.version })
  }
}

function backupBeforeMigrations(database: Database.Database, databasePath: string, userDataDir: string): void {
  const hasMigrationTable = database
    .prepare("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = 'schema_migrations'")
    .get()
  if (!hasMigrationTable) return

  const applied = database.prepare('SELECT MAX(version) AS version FROM schema_migrations').get() as
    | { version: number | null }
    | undefined
  if ((applied?.version ?? 0) >= CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION) return

  const backupsDir = path.join(userDataDir, 'backups')
  fs.mkdirSync(backupsDir, { recursive: true })
  const backupPath = path.join(backupsDir, `pre-migration-${Date.now()}.sqlite3`)
  database.pragma('wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)')
  fs.copyFileSync(databasePath, backupPath)
  log.info('Pre-migration database backup created', { backupPath, fromVersion: applied?.version ?? 0, toVersion: CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION })

/**

 * `  1.    18375 [04:05.00]        0 [00:00.00]    no   no  2`
 * (length in sectors, then start sector).

export function parseCdparanoia(output: string): AudioCdToc {
  const tracks: AudioCdTrack[] = []
  for (const line of output.split('\n')) {
    const match = line.match(/^\s*(\d+)\.\s+(\d+)\s+\[[\d:.]+\]\s+(\d+)\s+\[/)

  return { tracks, leadoutSector: last ? last.startSector + last.sectors : 0 }
}

/**
 * Rips a single CDDA track to a WAV file for playback. Uses cdparanoia's error-correcting read
 * (slower than a plain dd/dump, but tolerant of the scratched/aging discs this app catalogs).
 */
export async function ripCddaTrack(devicePath: string, trackNumber: number, outputPath: string): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await execFileAsync('cdparanoia', ['-d', devicePath, String(trackNumber), outputPath])
  } catch (err) {
    if (isMissingBinary(err)) throw new Error(MISSING_TOOLS_MESSAGE)
    if (isEmptyDrive(err)) throw new Error(NO_DISC_MESSAGE)
    throw new Error(`Could not rip track ${trackNumber}: ${(err as Error).message}`)
  }
}

import { app, protocol } from 'electron'
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'
import { Readable } from 'node:stream'
import { getFileMeta } from '../db/fileRepository'
import { getMediaItem } from '../db/mediaRepository'
import { listConnectedDevices } from '../devices/deviceDetection'
import { ripCddaTrack } from '../scanning/audioCd'
import { resolveLivePath } from './files'

/** Custom scheme the renderer's <audio> element streams cataloged audio files through. */
export const AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME = 'discdock-media'

// Rips are cached on disk (one physical disc per media item) and de-duped across concurrent requests.
const cddaCacheDir = (): string => path.join(app.getPath('userData'), 'cdda-cache')
const ripsInFlight = new Map<string, Promise<string>>()

function guessAudioMimeType(filePath: string): string {
  const ext = filePath.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase()
  switch (ext) {
    case 'mp3':
      return 'audio/mpeg'
    case 'wav':
      return 'audio/wav'
    case 'flac':
      return 'audio/flac'
    case 'ogg':
      return 'audio/ogg'
    case 'm4a':
    case 'aac':
      return 'audio/aac'
    case 'opus':
      return 'audio/opus'
    default:
      return 'application/octet-stream'
  }
}

/** Finds the currently connected optical drive backing this media item, if any. */
async function resolveOpticalDevicePath(mediaId: number): Promise<string> {
  const item = getMediaItem(mediaId)
  if (!item) throw new Error(`Media item ${mediaId} not found`)
  if (!item.deviceFingerprint) throw new Error(`"${item.label}" is not linked to a device`)

  const devices = await listConnectedDevices()
  const device = devices.find((d) => (d.uuid ?? d.devicePath) === item.deviceFingerprint)
  if (!device) throw new Error(`"${item.label}" is not currently inserted — insert the disc and try again`)
  return device.devicePath
}

/** Rips (or reuses a cached rip of) a CDDA track, returning the path to the resulting WAV file. */
async function getOrRipCddaTrack(mediaId: number, trackNumber: number): Promise<string> {
  const cacheKey = `${mediaId}:${trackNumber}`
  const cacheDir = cddaCacheDir()
  const cachePath = path.join(cacheDir, `media-${mediaId}-track-${trackNumber}.wav`)
  if (fs.existsSync(cachePath)) return cachePath

  const inFlight = ripsInFlight.get(cacheKey)
  if (inFlight) return inFlight

  const ripPromise = (async () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(cacheDir, { recursive: true })
    const devicePath = await resolveOpticalDevicePath(mediaId)
    const tempPath = `${cachePath}.partial`
    await ripCddaTrack(devicePath, trackNumber, tempPath)
    fs.renameSync(tempPath, cachePath)
    return cachePath
  })()

  ripsInFlight.set(cacheKey, ripPromise)
  try {
    return await ripPromise
  } finally {
    ripsInFlight.delete(cacheKey)
  }
}

/** Serves a file from disk with Range support so <audio> can seek. */
function streamFile(resolvedPath: string, mimeType: string, request: Request): Response {
  const stat = fs.statSync(resolvedPath)

  let start = 0
  let end = stat.size - 1
  let status = 200
  const headers: Record<string, string> = { 'Content-Type': mimeType, 'Accept-Ranges': 'bytes' }

  const range = request.headers.get('range')
  if (range) {
    const match = /bytes=(\d*)-(\d*)/.exec(range)
    if (match && (match[1] || match[2])) {
      if (match[1]) start = Number(match[1])
      if (match[2]) end = Number(match[2])
      status = 206
      headers['Content-Range'] = `bytes ${start}-${end}/${stat.size}`
    }
  }

  headers['Content-Length'] = String(end - start + 1)
  const nodeStream = fs.createReadStream(resolvedPath, { start, end })
  return new Response(Readable.toWeb(nodeStream) as ReadableStream, { status, headers })
}

/** Must be called before app.whenReady(), pairs with registerAudioStreamProtocol(). */
export function registerAudioStreamSchemePrivileges(): void {
  protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged([
    { scheme: AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME, privileges: { stream: true, supportFetchAPI: true, corsEnabled: true } }
  ])
}

/**
 * Serves cataloged audio files at discdock-media://<mediaId>/<encoded relative path>. Real files
 * stream straight from the mounted device; CDDA tracks (raw audio-CD sectors, no underlying file)
 * are ripped to a cached WAV via cdparanoia on first request, then streamed the same way.
 */
export function registerAudioStreamProtocol(): void {
  protocol.handle(AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME, async (request) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(request.url)
      const mediaId = Number(url.hostname)
      const filePath = decodeURIComponent(url.pathname.slice(1))
      if (!Number.isInteger(mediaId) || mediaId <= 0 || !filePath) {
        return new Response('Invalid audio request', { status: 400 })
      }

      const meta = getFileMeta(mediaId, filePath)
      if (!meta || meta.kind !== 'audio') return new Response('Not an audio file', { status: 403 })

      if (meta.extension === 'cdda') {
        if (meta.trackNumber == null) return new Response('Track has no track number recorded', { status: 500 })
        const wavPath = await getOrRipCddaTrack(mediaId, meta.trackNumber)
        return streamFile(wavPath, 'audio/wav', request)
      }

      const resolved = await resolveLivePath(mediaId, filePath)
      return streamFile(resolved, guessAudioMimeType(resolved), request)
    } catch (err) {
      return new Response(`Audio stream error: ${(err as Error).message}`, { status: 404 })
    }
  })
}

/**
 * Looks up a single cataloged file's playback-relevant metadata. CDDA tracks have kind 'audio'
 * but no underlying file — callers use extension/trackNumber to route them through ripping
 * instead of the normal mounted-filesystem path.
 */
export function getFileMeta(
  mediaItemId: number,
  filePath: string
): { kind: string; extension: string | null; trackNumber: number | null } | null {
  const row = getDb()
    .prepare(
      `SELECT kind, extension, track_number FROM file_record
       WHERE media_item_id = @mediaItemId AND path = @filePath AND is_directory = 0`
    )
    .get({ mediaItemId, filePath }) as { kind: string; extension: string | null; track_number: number | null } | undefined
  if (!row) return null
  return { kind: row.kind, extension: row.extension, trackNumber: row.track_number }
}
  return row.kind
}

## CDDA (true Audio CD) playback implemented (2026-08-19)
- Migration v7 added `file_record.track_number` (electron/db/index.ts) so a cataloged `.cdda`
  entry can be mapped back to its physical track for ripping; set in scanManager.ts's
  upsertFileRecord call, read via the new `getFileMeta()` in fileRepository.ts (replaces the old

- electron/ipc/mediaStream.ts's discdock-media:// protocol handler now branches on
  `extension === 'cdda'`: rips to `<userData>/cdda-cache/media-<id>-track-<n>.wav` (ripped to a
  `.partial` file then renamed, so a half-finished rip is never served), cached indefinitely,
  de-duped across concurrent requests via an in-memory `ripsInFlight` Map. Device to rip from is
  resolved by matching the media item's `deviceFingerprint` against `listConnectedDevices()`
  (same pattern as files.ts's resolveLivePath) — errors clearly if the disc isn't currently

- Ripping a whole track before the first response byte means playback start is NOT instant —

  `isBuffering` (audio 'waiting'/'canplay'/'playing' events) and PlayerBar shows "Ripping track…"
  meanwhile. This is a known UX tradeoff for v1; a future improvement would stream progressively
  instead of rip-then-serve.
- Renderer no longer excludes `.cdda` entries from Play buttons/queues (MediaDetail.tsx Browse
  tab, MediaLibrary.tsx context menu) now that they're genuinely playable.

## CDDA playback is now implemented

**How it works:**
- Added a  DB column (migration v7) so cataloged CDDA track entries map back to their physical track.
- `audioCd.ts` gained , which shells out to `cdparanoia -d <device> <track> <outFile>` (confirmed installed at `cdparanoia`).
- The `discdock-media://` streaming protocol now branches: real files stream straight from the mounted path as before; `.cdda` tracks get ripped on first request to a cached WAV under `<userData>/cdda-cache/`, then served the same way. Rips are cached indefinitely and de-duped if you click Play twice quickly. It resolves the current physical drive from the media item's device fingerprint and errors clearly if the disc isn't inserted.
- Play buttons in Media Library and Media Detail no longer exclude Audio CD tracks.
- Since ripping the whole track happens before playback starts, there's a real delay (roughly real-time speed) — the player bar now shows **"Ripping track…"** while that happens, via a new  state.

**Known trade-off:** it rips-then-serves rather than streaming progressively, so a 4-minute track takes roughly 4 minutes before you hear it the first time; subsequent plays are instant (cached). Progressive/streaming ripping would be a further improvement if that delay matters. Full build is clean — try playing an audio CD now.

async function resolveOpticalDevicePath(mediaId: number): Promise<string> {
  const item = getMediaItem(mediaId)
  if (!item) throw new Error(`Media item ${mediaId} not found`)
  if (!item.deviceFingerprint) throw new Error(`"${item.label}" is not linked to a device`)

  const devices = await listConnectedDevices()
  const device = devices.find((d) => (d.uuid ?? d.devicePath) === item.deviceFingerprint)
  if (!device) throw new Error(`"${item.label}" is not currently inserted — insert the disc and try again`)
  return device.devicePath
}

/**
 * Rips a single CDDA track to a WAV file for playback. Uses cdparanoia's error-correcting read
 * (slower than a plain dd/dump, but tolerant of the scratched/aging discs this app catalogs).
 */
export async function ripCddaTrack(devicePath: string, trackNumber: number, outputPath: string): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await execFileAsync('cdparanoia', ['-d', devicePath, String(trackNumber), outputPath])
  } catch (err) {
    if (isMissingBinary(err)) throw new Error(MISSING_TOOLS_MESSAGE)
    if (isEmptyDrive(err)) throw new Error(NO_DISC_MESSAGE)
    throw new Error(`Could not rip track ${trackNumber}: ${(err as Error).message}`)
  }

protocol } from 'electron'
import fs from 'node:fs'
import { Readable } from 'node:stream'
import { getFileKind } from '../db/fileRepository'
import { resolveLivePath } from './files'

/** Custom scheme the renderer's <audio> element streams cataloged audio files through. */
export const AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME = 'discdock-media'

function guessAudioMimeType(filePath: string): string {
  const ext = filePath.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase()
  switch (ext) {
    case 'mp3':
      return 'audio/mpeg'
    case 'wav':
      return 'audio/wav'
    case 'flac':
      return 'audio/flac'
    case 'ogg':
      return 'audio/ogg'
    case 'm4a':
    case 'aac':
      return 'audio/aac'
    case 'opus':
      return 'audio/opus'
    default:
      return 'application/octet-stream'
  }
}

/** Must be called before app.whenReady(), pairs with registerAudioStreamProtocol(). */
export function registerAudioStreamSchemePrivileges(): void {
  protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged([
    { scheme: AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME, privileges: { stream: true, supportFetchAPI: true, corsEnabled: true } }
  ])
}

/**
 * Serves cataloged audio files at discdock-media://<mediaId>/<encoded relative path>, with
 * Range support so <audio> can seek. Only files cataloged with kind 'audio' are served.
 */
export function registerAudioStreamProtocol(): void {
  protocol.handle(AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME, async (request) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(request.url)
      const mediaId = Number(url.hostname)
      const filePath = decodeURIComponent(url.pathname.slice(1))
      if (!Number.isInteger(mediaId) || mediaId <= 0 || !filePath) {
        return new Response('Invalid audio request', { status: 400 })
      }
      if (getFileKind(mediaId, filePath) !== 'audio') {
        return new Response('Not an audio file', { status: 403 })
      }

      const resolved = await resolveLivePath(mediaId, filePath)
      const stat = await fs.promises.stat(resolved)

      let start = 0
      let end = stat.size - 1
      let status = 200
      const headers: Record<string, string> = {
        'Content-Type': guessAudioMimeType(resolved),
        'Accept-Ranges': 'bytes'
      }

      const range = request.headers.get('range')
      if (range) {
        const match = /bytes=(\d*)-(\d*)/.exec(range)
        if (match && (match[1] || match[2])) {
          if (match[1]) start = Number(match[1])
          if (match[2]) end = Number(match[2])
          status = 206
          headers['Content-Range'] = `bytes ${start}-${end}/${stat.size}`
        }
      }

      headers['Content-Length'] = String(end - start + 1)
      const nodeStream = fs.createReadStream(resolved, { start, end })
      return new Response(Readable.toWeb(nodeStream) as ReadableStream, { status, headers }

/**
 * Looks up a single cataloged file's kind, used to gate playback to real audio-kind entries.
 * Audio-CD scans catalog synthetic `.cdda` track placeholders with no underlying file, so those
 * are excluded even though they're marked kind 'audio'.
 */
export function getFileKind(mediaItemId: number, filePath: string): string | null {
  const row = getDb()
    .prepare(
      `SELECT kind, extension FROM file_record
       WHERE media_item_id = @mediaItemId AND path = @filePath AND is_directory = 0`
    )
    .get({ mediaItemId, filePath }) as { kind: string; extension: string | null } | undefined
  if (!row || row.extension === 'cdda') return null

    directoryFileCount: row.directory_file_count,
    directorySizeBytes: row.directory_size_bytes,
    modifiedAtSrc: row.modified_at_src,
    durationSeconds: row.duration_seconds
  }))
}

/**
 * Looks up a single cataloged file's kind, used to gate playback to real audio-kind entries.
 * Audio-CD scans catalog synthetic `.cdda` track placeholders with no underlying file, so those
 * are excluded even though they're marked kind 'audio'.
 */
export function getFileKind(mediaItemId: number, filePath: string): string | null {
  const row = getDb()
    .prepare(
      `SELECT kind, extension FROM file_record
       WHERE media_item_id = @mediaItemId AND path = @filePath AND is_directory = 0`
    )
    .get({ mediaItemId, filePath }) as { kind: string; extension: string | null } | undefined
  if (!row || row.extension === 'cdda') return null
  return row.kind
```

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Fully reverted — CDDA playback is back to showing "DiscDock doesn't support playing CDDA discs directly yet," and full build is clean. You're right that I should have flagged the rip-then-serve delay as a tradeoff before building it. Fair point, noted for next time.

Here are real alternatives, each with different tradeoffs:

**1. Progressive/streaming rip (pipe instead of rip-to-file)**
Stream `cdparanoia`'s stdout directly into the HTTP response as it's produced, instead of waiting for the whole track. Playback can start almost immediately (a couple seconds of buffering), like normal streaming audio. Downside: seeking ahead of the currently-ripped point isn't possible until that point has been ripped — so scrubbing forward mid-playback is limited.

**2. Background pre-rip on disc scan**
As soon as an audio CD is scanned/cataloged, kick off ripping all tracks in the background (or just track 1, then the rest). By the time the user actually presses Play, it's often already cached and plays instantly. Downside: uses drive/CPU time even if the user never plays anything; still has a wait if they hit Play immediately after scanning.

**3. Click-to-rip with visible progress, no fake "later"**
Keep rip-then-serve, but make the wait honest and bounded: show a real progress bar/percentage/ETA (cdparanoia reports progress) instead of a vague spinner, and let the user browse elsewhere in the app while it rips in the background, notifying when ready. Doesn't remove the wait, but removes the "hesitation" feeling of silence.

**4. Faster, less error-corrected rip**
Drop cdparanoia's full error-correction (e.g., a plain `-Z`/burst mode, or a simpler tool) for a much faster read closer to drive speed rather than ~1x realtime. Cuts wait time significantly but is less robust against scratched/aging discs, which is a real concern for a disc-cataloging app.

Which direction do you want to pursue (or a combination, e.g. #1 + #4)?

_**User (2026-08-19 21:27:28Z)**_

and we would use a different plugin altogether for mp3 and other compressed formats?

---

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

No new plugin needed for MP3/compressed formats — that part is already done and separate from this discussion.

**Why they're different problems:**
- **MP3/AAC/FLAC/OGG files** (on a data disc or already-ripped folder): these are real files with real bytes on the filesystem. Chromium's built-in `<audio>` element already decodes MP3/AAC/etc. natively — no plugin, no extra tooling. That's the Phase 1 implementation already shipped and working (streamed via the `discdock-media://` protocol straight from the mounted path).
- **True Audio CD (CDDA)**: there is no file at all — it's raw redbook PCM audio sitting in sectors on the disc, addressable only by an optical drive command, not a filesystem path. `cdparanoia` (or an alternative like `cdda2wav`) is only needed to *extract* those raw sectors into an actual audio stream/file in the first place. Once extracted (whether via streaming pipe or full rip-to-file), it's raw PCM/WAV — again just handled natively by `<audio>`, no plugin required there either.

So the "different plugin/tool" question only applies to the *extraction* step for physical audio CDs. `cdparanoia` is the standard tool for that on Linux; alternatives are `cdda2wav`/`icedax` (similar tradeoffs) or `libcdio`'s ripping utilities — none of them avoid the fundamental "read raw sectors off a spinning disc" time cost, which is what options 1–4 above are trying to work around, not replace.

Want me to go with a specific one of those four (or a combo) for the actual implementation?

import { execFile } from 'node:child_process'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { promisify } from 'node:util'
import { nativeImage } from 'electron'
import type { AudioCdMetadata, AudioCdToc, AudioCdTrack } from '../../shared/types'

const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile)

const CDDA_BYTES_PER_SECTOR = 2352
const CDDA_SECTORS_PER_SECOND = 75
// Audio CD track offsets are expressed from the start of the disc, which begins at sector 150.
const CDDA_LEADIN_SECTORS = 150

const MISSING_TOOLS_MESSAGE =
  'Reading audio CDs needs a CD tool that DiscDock does not bundle. Install one, then try again:\n' +
  '  Debian/Ubuntu/Mint:  sudo apt install libcdio-utils cdparanoia\n' +
  '  Fedora/RHEL:         sudo dnf install libcdio cdparanoia\n' +
  '  Arch:                sudo pacman -S libcdio cdparanoia'

const NO_DISC_MESSAGE = 'No disc detected in the drive — insert an audio CD and try again.'

/** True when the failure is "the binary is not installed" rather than a read error. */
function isMissingBinary(err: unknown): boolean {
  const error = err as NodeJS.ErrnoException & { stderr?: string }
  return error.code === 'ENOENT' || /not found/i.test(error.stderr ?? '')
}

function isEmptyDrive(err: unknown): boolean {
  const detail = (err as Error & { stderr?: string; stdout?: string })
  const text = `${detail.stderr ?? ''}${detail.stdout ?? ''}${detail.message ?? ''}`
  return /no medium|no disc|can't get first track|not ready/i.test(text)
}

function sectorsToSeconds(sectors: number): number {
  return Math.round(sectors / CDDA_SECTORS_PER_SECOND)
}

function toTrack(trackNumber: number, startSector: number, sectors: number, isAudio: boolean): AudioCdTrack {
  return {
    trackNumber,
    startSector,
    sectors,
    durationSeconds: sectorsToSeconds(sectors),
    sizeBytes: sectors * CDDA_BYTES_PER_SECTOR,
    isAudio
  }
}

/** Builds a canonical 44-byte PCM WAV header. dataSizeBytes is known upfront from the disc's TOC. */
export function buildWavHeader(dataSizeBytes: number): Buffer {
  const header = Buffer.alloc(44)
  const byteRate = CDDA_SAMPLE_RATE * CDDA_CHANNELS * (CDDA_BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8)
  const blockAlign = CDDA_CHANNELS * (CDDA_BITS_PER_SAMPLE / 8)

  header.write('RIFF', 0, 'ascii')
  header.writeUInt32LE(36 + dataSizeBytes, 4)
  header.write('WAVE', 8, 'ascii')
  header.write('fmt ', 12, 'ascii')
  header.writeUInt32LE(16, 16)
  header.writeUInt16LE(1, 20) // PCM
  header.writeUInt16LE(CDDA_CHANNELS, 22)
  header.writeUInt32LE(CDDA_SAMPLE_RATE, 24)
  header.writeUInt32LE(byteRate, 28)
  header.writeUInt16LE(blockAlign, 32)
  header.writeUInt16LE(CDDA_BITS_PER_SAMPLE, 34)
  header.write('data', 36, 'ascii')
  header.writeUInt32LE(dataSizeBytes, 40)
  return header
}

/**
 * Spawns cdparanoia ripping one track as raw PCM to stdout so playback can start as bytes
 * arrive, instead of waiting for the whole track to be ripped to a file first. The caller owns
 * the process: it must consume/pipe stdout, watch stderr/'error'/'exit' for failures, and kill
 * it on client disconnect.
 */
export function spawnCddaTrackStream(devicePath: string, trackNumber: number): ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams {
  return spawn('cdparanoia', ['-r', '-d', devicePath, String(trackNumber), '-'])
}

```
playback-relevant metadata. CDDA tracks have kind 'audio'
 * but no underlying file — callers use extension/trackNumber/sizeBytes to route them through
 * live ripping instead of the normal mounted-filesystem path.
 */
export function getFileMeta(
  mediaItemId: number,
  filePath: string
): { kind: string; extension: string | null; trackNumber: number | null; sizeBytes: number } | null {
  const row = getDb()
    .prepare(
      `SELECT kind, extension, track_number, size_bytes FROM file_record
       WHERE media_item_id = @mediaItemId AND path = @filePath AND is_directory = 0`
    )
    .get({ mediaItemId, filePath }) as
    | { kind: string; extension: string | null; track_number: number | null; size_bytes: number }
    | undefined
  if (!row) return null
  return { kind: row.kind, extension: row.extension, trackNumber: row.track_number, sizeBytes: row.size_bytes }

import { getFileMeta } from '../db/fileRepository'

import { listConnectedDevices } from '../devices/deviceDetection'
import { buildWavHeader, spawnCddaTrackStream } from '../scanning/audioCd'
import { log } from '../logging'
import { resolveLivePath } from './files'

/** Custom scheme the renderer's <audio> element streams cataloged audio files through. */
export const AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME = 'discdock-media'

function guessAudioMimeType(filePath: string): string {
  const ext = filePath.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase()
  switch (ext) {
    case 'mp3':
      return 'audio/mpeg'
    case 'wav':
      return 'audio/wav'
    case 'flac':
      return 'audio/flac'
    case 'ogg':
      return 'audio/ogg'
    case 'm4a':
    case 'aac':
      return 'audio/aac'
    case 'opus':
      return 'audio/opus'
    default:
      return 'application/octet-stream'
  }
}

/** Finds the currently connected optical drive backing this media item, if any. */
async function resolveOpticalDevicePath(mediaId: number): Promise<string> {
  const item = getMediaItem(mediaId)
  if (!item) throw new Error(`Media item ${mediaId} not found`)
  if (!item.deviceFingerprint) throw new Error(`"${item.label}" is not linked to a device`)

  const devices = await listConnectedDevices()
  const device = devices.find((d) => (d.uuid ?? d.devicePath) === item.deviceFingerprint)
  if (!device) throw new Error(`"${item.label}" is not currently inserted — insert the disc and try again`)
  return device.devicePath
}

/**
 * Streams a CDDA track live: a WAV header (data size known upfront from the TOC) followed by
 * cdparanoia's raw PCM output, piped through as it's produced. Playback starts almost
 * immediately instead of waiting for the whole track to be ripped first. Not seekable ahead of
 * what's been streamed so far — the process is killed if the client disconnects.
 */
function streamCddaTrack(devicePath: string, trackNumber: number, dataSizeBytes: number, request: Request): Response {
  const child = spawnCddaTrackStream(devicePath, trackNumber)
  const body = new PassThrough()
  body.write(buildWavHeader(dataSizeBytes))
  child.stdout.pipe(body)

  let stderrTail = ''
  child.stderr.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => {
    stderrTail = (stderrTail + chunk.toString()).slice(-2000)
  })
  child.on('error', (err) => body.destroy(err))
  child.on('exit', (code) => {
    if (code !== 0 && code !== null) log.warn(`cdparanoia (track ${trackNumber}) exited ${code}: ${stderrTail}`)
    body.end()
  })
  request.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => {
    child.kill('SIGTERM')
    body.destroy()
  })

  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    'Content-Type': 'audio/wav',
    'Content-Length': String(44 + dataSizeBytes),
    'Accept-Ranges': 'none'
  }
  return new Response(Readable.toWeb(body) as ReadableStream, { status: 200, headers })
}

/** Must be called before app.whenReady(), pairs with registerAudioStreamProtocol(). */
export function registerAudioStreamSchemePrivileges(): void {
  protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged([
    { scheme: AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME, privileges: { stream: true, supportFetchAPI: true, corsEnabled: true } }
  ])
}

 * no underlying file) are streamed live from cdparanoia (see streamCddaTrack).

export function registerAudioStreamProtocol(): void {
  protocol.handle(AUDIO_STREAM_SCHEME, async (request) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(request.url)
      const mediaId = Number(url.hostname)
      const filePath = decodeURIComponent(url.pathname.slice(1))
      if (!Number.isInteger(mediaId) || mediaId <= 0 || !filePath) {
        return new Response('Invalid audio request', { status: 400 })

      const meta = getFileMeta(mediaId, filePath)
      if (!meta || meta.kind !== 'audio') return new Response('Not an audio file', { status: 403 })

      if (meta.extension === 'cdda') {
        if (meta.trackNumber == null) return new Response('Track has no track number recorded', { status: 500 })

        return streamCddaTrack(devicePath, meta.trackNumber, meta.sizeBytes, request

## CDDA (true Audio CD) playback — progressive streaming (2026-08-19)
- User chose alternative (1) after the rip-then-serve version was reverted: stream cdparanoia's

  `cdparanoia -r -d <device> <track> -` (raw PCM to stdout, no WAV header — cdparanoia can't
  write a correct header to a pipe since it doesn't know the size in advance). `buildWavHeader()`
  builds the 44-byte header ourselves using the fixed CDDA format (44.1kHz/16-bit/stereo) and the
  **exact** data length already known from the TOC (`file_record.size_bytes`), so the header is
  correct even though we haven't ripped anything yet.
- electron/ipc/mediaStream.ts's `streamCddaTrack()`: PassThrough stream = header bytes, then
  `child.stdout.pipe(body)`. Response has `Content-Length` (known upfront) but
  `Accept-Ranges: none` — seeking ahead of what's streamed so far is NOT supported yet (killed
  and restarted from scratch is the only option today); seeking backward within already-buffered
  audio still works via the browser's local buffer. `request.signal` abort (track skipped/closed)

  audio starts as soon as the first PCM bytes arrive rather than after the whole track rips.
- No on-disk caching in this version (each play re-invokes cdparanoia from scratch) — deferred,
  along with full seeking, per user's "we'll address [more of] ripping an audio CD later".
- NOT tested against real physical audio-CD hardware in this session (no disc available) — only
  verified via `npm run build` (full renderer+electron compile). Ask the user to test with a real
  audio CD before considering this done.

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Implemented. Summary:

**What changed:**
- `audioCd.ts`:  runs `cdparanoia -r -d <device> <track> -` piping raw PCM to stdout;  constructs a correct WAV header upfront using the exact track length already known from the disc's TOC (no need to rip first to know the size).
- `mediaStream.ts`: CDDA tracks now stream live — header + piped `cdparanoia` stdout — instead of rip-to-file. Playback should start in a couple seconds rather than waiting out the whole track. The spawned process is killed if the client disconnects/skips.
- Play buttons/menus in Media Library and Media Detail work for CDDA tracks again.
- Player bar shows a brief "Starting stream…" instead of the old "Ripping track…".

**Known limitations for this pass (per your "address later"):**
- No caching — replaying a track re-invokes `cdparanoia` from scratch each time.
- No seeking ahead of what's been streamed so far (seeking backward within already-buffered audio still works).

Full build (`npm run build`) is clean, but I haven't tested this against real audio-CD hardware — please try it with an actual disc and let me know what happens.
